Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
Kenneth found that design agents tend to write cryptic UI text: dense, mechanism-first phrases that read clearly only to the writer. On 2026-11-06 a cold-reader test showed that a fresh agent shown only screenshots catches most of these problems. It caught 14 of the 23 problems an expert review found on the first-launch flow, and 4 more partly. The method and the wording rule were written into `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md` (commit 8acb12318c on jusprin-newui), with pointers in `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

Kenneth's working rules for this:
- Design lives in Claude artifacts, mainly the JusPrin v2 canvas. `jusprin-newui` is the code branch.
- Several other sessions edit the canvas, and its canvas.json is one shared file. Never publish to it without coordinating with them.
- JusPrin commits now land on `jusprin-newui-integration`, but this task commits nothing.
- The Mac is shared, so follow the build rules in `AGENTS.md`: check load first, use -j4, run one build per build directory, and reuse an existing build.
- Temporary working docs stay untracked.

Task:
Sweep every fork-owned JusPrin screen against the design guidelines in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md`. List where a first-time or ordinary user would misread the text or get stuck, and propose a fix for each. Report only: change no code and publish nothing to the JusPrin v2 canvas until Kenneth has picked which fixes to take.

Scope: every screen JusPrin draws itself, meaning the code under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added in OrcaSlicer-owned files. That covers the Agent page (project chat, printer chat, chat list, turn activity, setup card, composer, error and recovery states), Preferences (Agent, Account, Appearance, 3D view, Projects & files, Updates), Home (project gallery, agent card, printer cards and status), the native shell (header, printer and filament chips and their menus, add-printer form, plates pane), check print and the slice report, print history, calibration, and File › Import from OrcaSlicer. Start by making the full list of screens and states from the code, and check it against the boards on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Stock OrcaSlicer screens are out of scope; check fork ownership with `git blame` as `AGENTS.md` describes. The first-launch screens were swept on 2026-11-06 and their fixes are being built now, so include them only to check that no new problems came in.

Method: follow the guidelines' steps.
- Capture real screenshots of each screen in its real states, from coherent user paths. Mixed paths or made-up data that doesn't agree across screens make the cold reader report false contradictions.
- Use the fake-host page fixture for the web pages and a scratch copy of the built app with its own `--datadir` for native screens. Never drive another JusPrin instance.
- Run the cold-reader check: give a fresh agent only the screenshots, with neutral file names and one line of context.
- Then read each screen yourself against the wording rule's five patterns, and against the code, for claims the screen makes that aren't true.

Done looks like this: one report published as a Claude artifact, grouped by screen. Each problem shows the screenshot, the exact current text, what a person would misread or where they'd get stuck, and a proposed rewording or change, marked as a proposal. Each proposal is checked against the code as true. Next to each problem, say whether the cold reader caught it or only your own reading did. End the report with the decisions that are Kenneth's to make, written as "Decision needed" paragraphs. Then tell Kenneth the link.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_92343330-5a7c-41c6-b491-f5068483611f

# JusPrin design guidelines

**Status:** Canonical guidance for `jusprin-newui` on how a screen gets designed and checked, and on the words it shows. The visual system (tokens, type, color, components, logo) lives in [Design system](design-system.md); this document does not repeat it.

Design agents tend to write on-screen text that only they can read. The agent knows how the screen works, so a line like "The sixth digit signs you in." reads clearly to it and to any reviewer who knows the same. A person opening the app for the first time has to decode it, and often can't. The First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15, 2026-11-06) found 23 places on the first launch where a newcomer would misread or stall, and most of them were wording. The rules below exist to stop that at the source and to catch what still gets through.

## How a screen gets designed and checked

1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "Until you add yours, files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer and may not print on other printers."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.

`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming

proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].
=== scratch-app-driving-traps.md
---
name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.
=== live-test-built-app-on-mac.md
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:

live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"

gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma

64	On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.
65	
66	**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.
67	
68	**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.
69	
70	**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.
71	
72	**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

98	name: scratch-app-driving-traps
99	description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
100	metadata:
101	  node_type: memory
102	  type: reference
103	  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
104	  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
105	---
106	
107	Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).
108	
109	- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
110	- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
111	- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
112	- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
113	- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
114	- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
115	- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
116	- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

118	---
119	name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
120	description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
121	metadata: 
122	  node_type: memory
123	  type: project
124	  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
125	  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
126	---
127	
128	Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.
129	
130	**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.
131	
132	The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.
133	
134	**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.
135	
136	**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].
137	
138	**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
139	2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
140	`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
141	`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
142	app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
143	a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
144	on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
145	the harness had opened on the Acer.
146	
147	Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
148	(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
149	captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
150	not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
151	"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.
152	
153	The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
154	read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
155	and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
156	evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
157	being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
158	concluding anything about the app.
159	
160	**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
161	`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
162	(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
163	`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
164	the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
165	
166	**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
167	`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
168	`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
169	all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
170	directory — the directory alone is not enough.
171	
172	**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.
173	
174	**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.
175	
176	**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.
177	
178	**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
179	against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
180	first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
181	agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
182	had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
183	`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
184	all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
185	treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
186	`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
187	rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.
188	
189	**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
190	"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
191	reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
192	display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
193	sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
194	button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
195	until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].
196	
197	**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).
198	
199	**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.
200	
201	**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

description: Test host behaviour in the real built app without screen control — point JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL at a copy of the built page with an injected script that logs envelopes to a local http.server and posts messages itself.

2026-10-21 (saved-key work, branch claude/api-key-saved-state): Kenneth declined computer-use control of the app, and the Remove path's AppConfig code only runs in the real app. What worked in ~2 minutes:

1. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject a `<script>` right after `<head>` that polls for `window.__jusprinBridge`, wraps its `deliver` to `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/log?'+JSON)` the envelopes of interest, and sends page messages with `window.wx.postMessage(JSON.stringify({protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge',version:1,id,type,payload}))`.
2. Serve the dir with `python3 -m http.server <port> --bind 127.0.0.1 > server.log`; the request log is the test output.
3. Launch the built binary directly: `JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/page.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 <app>/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with real *_api_key items deleted and TESTONLY keys added>`. The endpoint override keeps model-list and chat traffic off the real providers.
4. Read the data dir's JusPrin2.conf afterwards for persisted effects; delete the scratch data dir.

The fork's app bundle id is `io.jusprin.JusPrin` (not com.softfever3d.orca-slicer as [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] says). Related: [[fake-host-page-fixture]] (page-only states), [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

**Screenshots without screen control (2026-10-21):** add a `snap` command that POSTs `document.documentElement.outerHTML` (mark `document.activeElement` with `data-visual-focus` first) to a tiny local receiver, then strip `<script>`s, replace `:focus-visible` with `[data-visual-focus]`, pin `html,body` to the captured width (headless Chrome has a minimum window width) and screenshot. Keep the page running: the web view's timers stop ~10 s after the window loses visibility, so front the app by pid with `osascript … set frontmost` before every step and run `caffeinate -u -d -t 600`. The app follows the macOS appearance, not `dark_color_mode`; for dark captures deliver an `appearance: dark` envelope to the page and reapply it after any full `state` (a chat turn resends it). A stand-in provider (`JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` → local server that hangs while a flag file exists, else answers 401) produces "checking" and "rejected" for real.
description: "Drive \"open a file\" in a scratch copy of the built app with no screen control — AppleScript open addressed to the copy's path works; hidden Home page timers don't run; always override the model endpoint first."

2026-10-28 (phantom edit rows, critique 1B-02): Kenneth declined computer-use control of the app. What worked for "open a file in the running app" (the Finder path → `GUI_App::MacOpenFiles` → `ShellController::take_opened_files`):

`osascript -e 'tell application "<scratch>/App.app" to open POSIX file "<file>"'` — addresses the copy by its bundle path, so it reaches that instance and not another session's `io.jusprin.JusPrin`. It prints "missing value" and works. `open -g -a <path> <file>` was unreliable (lsappinfo held stale dead entries for the same path); if you use it, add `--args --datadir <scratch>` so a fresh launch can't touch the real data folder.

Do NOT Finder-open a `.3mf` this way: with `single_instance` off, `MacOpenFiles` calls `start_new_slicer`, a second instance on the default (real) data dir.

The Home page's injected-script approach ([[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]) fails for Home actions while Prepare is showing: the hidden Home web view runs no timers. The Agent page snapshot (`snap` → outerHTML → headless Chrome) still works for screenshots.

Opening a model starts an automatic first agent turn with the saved key. Set `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1` before launching, or a live model call goes out (it did once that day). See [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]].

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

Where a first-time user gets stuck

I walked JusPrin’s first launch on every path I could reach and found 23 places a newcomer is likely to misread or stall. Each orange number marks the spot on the screenshot; the same number below says what is on screen, why it confuses, and a proposed fix.

The proposals are mine and nothing is decided. The app freeze after Import is left out because another session is fixing it.

The welcome screen

  1. 1

    The only buttons are “Continue with Google” and “Continue with email”. The line under them says “New or existing account, same door.”

    A new person looks for “Sign up” or “Create account” and finds neither, so they wonder whether they need an account from somewhere else first. You flagged this one.

    ProposalLead with signing up: the email button reads “Sign up free”, with a small “Already have an account? Sign in” link under it. Both still send the same email code; only the words change.

  2. 2

    Above the three boxes: “Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent.”

    The boxes are three ways to pay for or connect the agent, not ways of thinking. The person doesn’t know yet what the agent is, what Preferences is, or why they must choose now.

    ProposalSay what the choice is: “Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice.”

  3. 3

    “An Expert message is 5 credits.”

    “Expert” appears nowhere else on the screen, so the person can’t tell what 500 credits buys.

    ProposalSay it in things the person does, for example “500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent”. The number needs checking against real costs.

  4. 4

    “Your own API key — Free” and “Claude Code or Claude Desktop — Free · MCP server”.

    “API key” and “MCP server” are developer words. “Free” beside them makes the 500-credit offer look like the expensive choice, and an API key isn’t free: the person pays the AI company directly.

    ProposalFold both into one quieter link, “Use your own AI account instead”, and explain the two options on the screen it opens.

Signing in with email

  1. 5

    The card asks “How do you want to sign in?” and offers a Password box with “Forgot password”. The line that tells a new person what to do, “New here? The code makes your account.”, is the smallest text on the card.

    A new person has no password. A password box suggests they should already have one.

    ProposalShow only “Email me a 6-digit code” at first, with a small “Use a password instead” link for people who set one.

Typing the emailed code

  1. 6

    “The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device.”

    It reads like a riddle. It means the app signs you in as soon as you type the last digit, and you can open the email on your phone.

    Proposal“Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone.”

  2. 7

    “Use the browser instead”.

    Nothing says what happens in the browser. It means “sign in with Google instead”.

    Proposal“Sign in with Google instead”.

Waiting for Google

  1. 8

    “Finish signing in in your browser.”

    The doubled “in” reads as a typo.

    Proposal“Finish in your browser.”

The printer step, signed in

  1. 9

    “Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits”. Your screenshot showed the same line on the OrcaSlicer import screen.

    The person just got 500 credits, and the line doesn’t say so. “500 credits” after a dot reads like a balance they had before. You flagged this one.

    Proposal“You got 500 free credits for signing up.” with the email address on a smaller line under it.

  2. 10

    “OrcaSlicer printers in another folder? Choose the folder…”

    It shows to everyone the app found no OrcaSlicer folder for, which includes everyone who has never used OrcaSlicer.

    ProposalRemove it here. The File › Import › “Import from OrcaSlicer…” menu item covers this later, once it is built.

  3. 11

    “Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours.” The code shows that Skip installs OrcaSlicer’s “Generic Klipper Printer”: a 250 × 250 mm bed and Klipper G-code.

    A Bambu or Prusa owner who skips gets G-code that may not run on their printer or fit their bed, and nothing says so.

    ProposalSay what the stand-in is: “Until you add yours, files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer and may not print on other printers.”

Choosing a printer model

  1. 12

    After the model is chosen, Continue stays grey and nothing on screen says why. In my run it stayed grey for 84 seconds while the app read the printer’s filaments and plates in the background.

    The person thinks they missed a field, or that the app is broken. The Mac was heavily loaded by other builds at the time (load 21 on 12 cores), so a normal Mac is probably faster; I didn’t measure that.

    ProposalShow “Reading this printer’s settings…” with a spinner under the nozzle buttons while Continue waits.

Bringing printers from OrcaSlicer

  1. 13

    All eight printers come over together. There is no way to leave one out.

    People keep old printers in OrcaSlicer that they no longer own, and they all show up in JusPrin.

    ProposalA tick box per printer, all ticked to start.

  2. 14

    The screen doesn’t say which printer JusPrin will use after the import.

    With eight printers, the person can’t guess which one their next slice uses.

    Proposal“JusPrin starts with Bambu Lab P1S, the printer OrcaSlicer had selected.”

  3. 15

    “Start fresh”.

    It sounds like it erases something. It means “skip the import and pick my printer by hand”.

    Proposal“Choose my printer instead”.

  4. 16

    The folder path and “· 3 filaments” share one line, and the count breaks onto two lines at the far right.

    The count is easy to miss and the path means nothing to most people.

    Proposal“Also brings 3 filaments” on its own line, and the path in smaller text.

What the import brought

  1. 17

    One filament failed out of seven items, and the title says “Some settings need attention”.

    It sounds alarming, and it calls printers and filaments “settings”.

    Proposal“Imported from OrcaSlicer” as the title, with the one failure shown in its row.

  2. 18

    “Not imported · its base profile, Kingroon PLA Silk, isn’t in JusPrin”, and a “Retry failed items” button.

    “Base profile” is jargon, there is no next step, and Retry fails the same way for this reason.

    Proposal“This filament is built on Kingroon PLA Silk, which JusPrin doesn’t have.” Show Retry only for failures a retry can fix, such as a file that couldn’t be read.

  3. 19

    “OrcaSlicer’s own files were not changed.”

    It answers a worry nobody raised here. The screen before already said “OrcaSlicer keeps its own copy.”

    ProposalRemove it.

Home, not signed in

  1. 20

    The printer added a moment ago says “Not connected. No network connection is set up.”

    It reads like something went wrong while adding it.

    Proposal“Connect it to send prints straight from JusPrin” beside the Connect button, with no status word until a connection was tried.

  2. 21

    The “Set up the agent” card repeats the sign-in card but never says what the agent does or that signing up gives 500 credits.

    Someone who skipped the welcome has no reason to fill it in.

    ProposalOne line of why at the top: “Get 500 free credits and ask the agent to fix failed prints.”

Home, signed in

  1. 22

    The same 500 credits have three names: “Your first month: 500 credits” on the welcome, “500 credits” after signing in, and “First-month credits … Expires 4 Dec” here. The expiry date first appears on Home.

    People wonder whether these are different credits, and learn they expire only after signing up.

    ProposalOne name everywhere, and the expiry in the sign-up line: “You got 500 free credits, good until 4 December.”

  2. 23

    “JusPrin account · Connected”, above a printer that says “Not connected”.

    “Connected” is printer language. For an account it reads as if the account is linked to a device.

    Proposal“Signed in as new@example.com”.

How this was checked

  • A scratch copy of the current build ran with its own empty data folder and a copy of your OrcaSlicer folder. The welcome, the printer form, the OrcaSlicer list and Home after adding a printer are the real app.
  • Sign-in screens, signed-in screens and the import result are the real page with the app’s state set by hand. I didn’t create accounts on staging or run the import.
  • Not covered: native windows and menus, such as Preferences (opened by “Your own API key”), the folder chooser and OrcaSlicer’s own dialogs, because screen control wasn’t available.
  • Also seen, not a wording problem: pressing Continue on the printer step froze the app for about 108 seconds while it installed the printer. That looks like the same kind of freeze as the one after Import.
